dedupe_keys.name: nato sto tr msg 187 space weather environmental modelling 2025

description: This NATO Science and Technology Organization technical report, published in September 2025 by the MSG-187 task group of the NATO Modelling and Simulation Group, reviews space weather environmental modelling for defence and civil users. It explains space weather phenomena and national observing capabilities, lists organisations with responsibilities such as the World Meteorological Organization, the International Space Environment Service, the ITU, UNOOSA, ESA and the Asia-Oceania Space Weather Alliance, and describes impacts on GNSS, solar flare and radio burst effects and scintillation. It then covers modelling centres, NASA's Community Coordinated Modeling Center and ESA's Virtual Space Weather Modelling Centre, data sources for modelling, including a TIEGCM model run for 2000 to 2020, OMNIWeb, the Madrigal database and GFZ Potsdam Kp, database requirements, and a machine learning design for correlating space weather with processes on Earth. Coverage is global. Format and access: a free 86-page PDF from the NATO STO publications site. Licence: NATO STO distribution terms, not read. Caveats: it is a study report that points to data, not publishing new data. It helps hazard exposure and resilience studies find space weather models and data for GNSS and communications. Related catalogue records are OMNIWeb solar wind data and the GFZ Kp index.
